# Vendored / generated files

## pattern-spec-validate.generated.js

A precompiled schema validator for `schema/pattern-spec.v1.json`, generated by
`scripts/generate-schema-validator.mjs` using ajv's **standalone validation
code** feature. Loaded by `js/schema-validate.js`.

This replaced an earlier approach (BerryStudio-Upgrade-Plan WP-0.3) that
vendored ajv v6's UMD runtime build (`ajv6.min.js`) and called `ajv.compile()`
in the browser. That approach was abandoned during WP-1 after empirical
testing: ajv's runtime compiler builds every validator with `new Function(...)`
at call time, which throws under a strict CSP with no `'unsafe-eval'` in
`script-src` — confirmed by actually loading it in the browser and hitting
`EvalError: ... violates ... script-src ... 'unsafe-eval' is not an allowed
source`. Since WP-1's security requirements call for a real CSP (not a
theoretical one weakened back open for this one feature), the fix is ajv's own
documented answer for CSP-locked apps: compile the schema **once, offline**,
to plain generated JS with zero runtime code generation — no `eval`, no
`Function` constructor, no ajv runtime shipped to the browser at all. The
generated file here is exactly that: a single exported function
(`validate10`, aliased as the default/`validate` export) built entirely from
`if`/property-access statements, verified by direct grep to contain no
`new Function`/`eval` anywhere in its body.

**To regenerate** (only needed when `schema/pattern-spec.v1.json` changes):
```
npm install --no-save ajv
node scripts/generate-schema-validator.mjs
```
`ajv` itself is never a runtime dependency of the shipped app — it's a
dev-only code-generation tool, used once per schema change, exactly the way
`ajv6.min.js` used to be regenerated via `npm pack ajv@6` before this switch.
Do not hand-edit the generated file.
